comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm provides a qualified defined contribution plan in the U.S., primarily the JPMorgan Chase 401(k) Savings Plan covering substantially all U.S. employees, which allows pretax and Roth contributions and includes annual matching and pay credit contributions by the Firm.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan disclose qualified defined contribution plans in the U.S. that include employer matching contributions. Citi specifies matching contributions of up to 6% of eligible compensation, while JPMorgan confirms making 'annual matching... contributions' without specifying the percentage in this excerpt. Both disclosures note that the plans cover substantially all or eligible U.S. employees.

sentences.text: Under the Citi Retirement Savings Plan, eligible U.S. employees received matching contributions of up to 6% of their eligible compensation for 2024 and 2023, subject to statutory limits.
The most significant of these plans is the JPMorgan Chase 401(k) Savings Plan ("the 401(k) Savings Plan"), which covers substantially all U.S. employees.
The Firm makes annual matching and pay credit contributions to the 401(k) Savings Plan on behalf of eligible participants.

comparisons.peer_summary: U.S. employees meeting eligibility requirements may participate in the 401(k) plan and receive discretionary matching contributions, which were generally up to 4% (or 5% for certain compensation levels) of eligible pay in 2024 and 2023. Eligible employees with pay of $100,001 or less also received a fixed contribution of 2% of eligible pay, with all contributions included in the firm's 401(k) expense.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Morgan Stanley disclose specific matching contribution structures and a fixed contribution component tied to compensation thresholds. Citi provides matching contributions of up to 6% and a fixed contribution of up to 2% for employees earning $100,000 or less. Similarly, Morgan Stanley provides discretionary matching contributions (generally up to 4% or 5%) and a fixed contribution of 2% for eligible employees with pay less than or equal to $100,001. Both firms explicitly mention that contributions are invested according to participant directions.

sentences.text: Under the Citi Retirement Savings Plan, eligible U.S. employees received matching contributions of up to 6% of their eligible compensation for 2024 and 2023, subject to statutory limits.
In addition, for eligible employees whose eligible compensation is $100,000 or less, a fixed contribution of up to 2% of eligible compensation is provided.
All Company contributions are invested according to participants' individual elections.
The Firm generally matched eligible employee contributions up to the IRS limit at 4%, or 5% up to a certain compensation level, in 2024 and 2023.
Eligible employees with eligible pay less than or equal to $100,001 also received a fixed contribution equal to 2% of eligible pay.
Contributions are invested among available funds according to each participant's investment direction and are included in the Firm's 401(k) expense.
